title: introduce-cohort-sample-manifests-and-watermark-backed-change-drafter
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: onboarding teams asked for smaller, targeted sample sets for release notes and regressions that map to customer cohorts (large-enterprise, mobile-first, helpdesk). In addition we need a way to produce concise changelog drafts that preserve sample provenance but remove identifying tokens: a watermark-backed drafting flow that ties a compact diff summary to a sampled manifest. Design: add a CohortSample manifest (schema v2) that declares sample cohorts, deterministic seed, and retention/privacy tags; implement a watermark drafters subsystem that can generate compact changelog teasers (one-line impact bullets + representative sample snippets) tied to a sample manifest hash and signature. The drafter uses K-anonymized snippet trimming and an optional token-redaction pipeline. Implementation: 1) manifest schema and validation (manifest/v2) + CLI preview (onboard-sample preview --manifest-file). 2) sampling worker that generates cohort-specific sample packs and stores lightweight fingerprints to the model registry storage backend. 3) watermark drafters service that consumes a manifest hash and emits a compact markdown-ready changelog snippet, with an attached provenance token for audit and rollback tooling. 4) compatibility checks added to the onboard pipeline: sample-aware performance baseline query and a lightweight eval probe that runs up to 100 queries across cohorts. 5) telemetry hooks so Console can show per-cohort sample coverage and digest generation latency. Rollout: behind feature-flag onboard.cohort_samples + gradual opt-in for model curators. Docs: CLI docs, manifest schema reference, and a short how-to for product teams to craft cohorts. Security/privacy: default redaction on snippets, signing of manifest hashes, and ability to opt-out of storing raw snippets. This PR groups the work into a logical change set to enable concise, cohort-aware release notes and safer public previews.
commits_summary: 6 commits: add manifest schema v2 and validator; sampling worker and deterministic seed; watermark drafter service and unit tests; CLI preview; registry API hooks and small telemetry additions; changelog examples and docs
review_conversation: Initial review requested more explicit privacy defaults and stronger validation for deterministic seeds. I (author) pushed commit 3 to enforce seed ranges and add a manifest-level 'privacy: redact_by_default' boolean. Priya requested a telemetry opt-out flag; added 'manifest.telemetry.disabled' and updated docs. Diego asked for tighter unit tests around the drafter's redaction (edge cases: email-like tokens, long numeric strings) and suggested adding deterministic sampling tests; added those tests in commit 5. Liam asked about performance cost of the cohort probe; we added a cap (100 queries) and a circuit-breaker. Approvals: Priya approved on 2025-11-24, Diego approved after tests passed, Liam approved after perf verification.
release_notes: Add cohort sample manifests (schema v2) and a watermark-based changelog drafter. Enables per-cohort concise release notes, deterministic sampling for reproducible regressions, and privacy-safe teaser generation. Controlled rollout behind onboard.cohort_samples feature flag.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for manifest validation and drafter redaction. End-to-end pipeline tested locally with a small model snapshot. Perf probe capped at 100 queries per manifest; CI runs an integration scenario using a synthetic sample pack. Manual QA: verified CLI preview output, manifest signature validation, and Console telemetry panel entries.
perf_impact: Read path unchanged for serving. Onboard pipeline: sampling job adds ~3% CPU on the curator worker during generation windows, storage footprint increased by ~120KB per sampled manifest (fingerprints + metadata). Drafter generation latency ~120-250ms per manifest on a small instance; negligible for UX flows.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable feature-flag for internal curators. 2) Run opt-in pilot with two product teams for 2 weeks. 3) Monitor telemetry: manifest-generation latency, sample-coverage, and any redaction failures. 4) Gradual enablement for all curators with 48h rollback path and a flag to disable public snippet previews.
notes_for_changelog_automation: Drafter emits a stable teaser payload that the changelog assembler can consume; payload contains manifest_hash, short impact bullets, and anonymized sample snippets. The assembler will now prefer cohort teasers when available and fall back to existing delta summarizers.
audit_log: manifest:v2 created (hash: abc123... truncated) by maya.chan@redwood on 2025-11-12; drafter run id: drafter-20251124-17a; signatures verified. Sensitive content redaction flag set to true by default.
authors_notes: This change was intentionally split to keep the sampler and drafter logically separated so that downstream release assembly can consume either component independently. Follow-up work: add compact coverage badges in Console and auto-schedule cohort-based evictions for stale samples.
